inventory.test: preserves the auth user when the transaction outcome is ambiguous
inventory.reason: M1: CONFIRMED_ROLLBACK_SQLSTATE /^(22|23|42)\d{3}$/ -> /^(08|22|23|42)\d{3}$/ (mint-admin.ts:363). Mutant SURVIVED. Arbiter: this test's injected error is `new Error('write CONNECTION_CLOSED')` with no `code`, so confirmsRollback short-circuits at `typeof code === 'string'` and the regex is never evaluated — the mutation is not executed on this test's path, which is a claim about the ORACLE, not the mutant. No test anywhere reaches confirmsRollback with a class-08 or class-57 SQLSTATE and an absent reconciliation row.

Arbiter: the mutated line IS executed, but the test asserts a bare `.toThrow()` with no message matcher, and all three probes are <=8 chars, so the refusal it observes is indistinguishable from the exact-equality refusal at :261/:269. The oracle cannot attribute the throw to the pattern guard it is named for.

The assertion at mint-admin.test.ts:544 cannot see this mutant. Coverage is NOT lost: IV-08 kills the same mutant on the live schema. The defect is in this oracle.

findings.title: The Auth-API duplicate-email refusal — the plan's second 'independent closer' — has no test at all
findings.reason: plan §2 row (c′) and intake edge_cases both present TWO independent closers for the half-succeeded hand process: the read-only auth.users probe, and auth.admin.createUser's own duplicate-email error. Only the probe is tested. isDuplicateEmailError (:522-527) and the entire `created.error` arm (:581-595) are 0-covered — no test double ever returns an error from createUser. This matters most on the target the runbook actually names: the local and CI databases have no auth.users relation, so the probe reports `unavailable` and the createUser classifier is the ONLY closer left. Fix: one unit test per arm (code 'email_exists', status 422, an 'already registered' message, and a non-duplicate error -> status 'failed').
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not mutation-derived: an uncovered production hunk with no covering candidate is a P1 by Step 2. Verified by reading both suites and by an istanbul coverage run of mint-admin.ts at HEAD under both suites.

findings.title: 'The Supabase createUser call returns no user with no error' is a locked intake edge case with no test
findings.reason: intake edge_cases names it verbatim ('treated as a failure, not as a mint'). mint-admin.ts:597-604 is 0-covered. The sibling it copies, provision-auth-user.ts:67, exists precisely because hosted Supabase Auth does return { error: null, user: null }. Fix: one test asserting status 'failed' with orphanAuthId null.

findings.title: 'generateLink fails after the transaction committed' is a locked intake edge case with no test
findings.reason: intake edge_cases: 'the mint stands and the script tells the operator to re-issue a recovery link rather than re-mint'. mint-admin.ts:664-674 is 0-covered — every double returns a hashed_token. This is the arm that must return status 'minted' with recoveryUrl null; a regression that returned 'failed' here would tell an operator to re-run a script that already committed. Fix: one test with generateLink -> { error } and one with a missing hashed_token.

findings.title: confirmsRollback's class-08/57 ambiguity — the asymmetric safety property — has no oracle; a mutant that adds class 08 to the confirmed-rollback set survives
findings.reason: intake edge_cases defines the ambiguous set as 'no SQLSTATE, or class 08 / 57'. The one test named for that edge case ('preserves the auth user when the transaction outcome is ambiguous') injects a code-less Error, so it exercises only the first third. Mutating CONFIRMED_ROLLBACK_SQLSTATE to /^(08|22|23|42)\d{3}$/ survives the whole suite. The regression it would let through is the exact failure the design forbids: an 08007 transaction_resolution_unknown would confirm a rollback and delete the Auth identity behind a users row that committed. Fix: two tests — pgError('08007') and pgError('57014'), each with an empty reconciliation read, asserting deleteUser NOT called.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutation M1 survived. It is not executed on the candidate test's path (the injected error carries no `code`), so the inventory row is inconclusive/oracle rather than a confirmed survivor — a claim about the oracle. Not raised as P0 because the production code at HEAD is CORRECT; what is missing is the assertion that keeps it correct.

findings.title: Fragile assertion: 'refuses a confirmed ref that is not a full Supabase project ref' asserts only that something throws
findings.reason: The loop probes 'supabase', an 8-char slice and '' against a bare `.toThrow()` with no matcher. Every one of those is ALSO refused by the exact-equality checks at mint-admin.ts:261/:269, so the test passes whether or not the PROJECT_REF_PATTERN guard exists at all — proved by mutating all three `{20}` quantifiers to `{16,}` and watching it stay green. Behavioural replacement: assert the message the guard owns, `.toThrow(/must be a complete Supabase project ref/)`, and add a 19-char probe so the length contract is actually exercised.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutation M3 survived on an executed line. Archetype 1 (a proxy assertion that passes while the bug exists).

findings.title: Fragile assertion: `inTransaction` is a time-window flag, not a connection identity, so the audit write can leave the transaction undetected
findings.reason: mock-sql stamps `inTransaction: isInTransaction()` (worker/__tests__/helpers/mock-sql.ts:134) — a module-level flag set for the duration of begin(). Any query issued during the callback is stamped true, including one issued on the OUTER sql handle. Mutating `writeAdminAuditLog(tx, …)` to `writeAdminAuditLog(sql, …)` — a real defect that would put the audit row on a separate pooled connection outside the transaction — leaves this test green. The test's own comment ('In the SAME transaction as the users INSERT') claims more than the assertion proves. Mitigating: the live-DB sibling ('commits the users row and its admin_audit_log row in one transaction') DOES kill the same mutant, so no coverage is lost; the remedy is to assert the tag identity (or to retitle the comment and point it at the live-DB suite as the real oracle).
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Mutation M12 survived the unit candidate and was killed by the integration candidate. The row is inconclusive/oracle rather than survived-confirmed-P0 precisely because the property IS covered elsewhere.

findings.title: Two documented target-parser behaviours are unreachable by any test: the direct `db.<ref>.` form and the unparseable-target refusal
findings.reason: refFromDatabaseTarget's JSDoc promises both forms — `db.<ref>.…` direct and `postgres.<ref>@…` pooler — and assertMintTarget's JSDoc promises 'an unparseable target is a refusal'. Coverage at HEAD: mint-admin.ts:208 (the direct branch) and :194 (refFromSupabaseUrl's invalid-URL return) never execute; every test uses a well-formed pooler descriptor with a 20-char ref. A regression that made either parser return the confirmRef instead of null would ship green. Fix: one test per form, plus one asserting a garbage dbTarget is refused with '(unparseable)' in the message.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Sibling hunt (Duty 4) over the guard's own documented input shapes, confirmed against the coverage run.

findings.title: readMintConfig, requireValue and the --env validation throw are entirely untested
findings.reason: resolveMintEnv (the pure mapping) is tested; readMintConfig — which selects .env.local vs .env.staging.local, raises the missing-file refusal (:163-167) and the four missing-variable refusals (:151-155) — is 0-covered, as is parseMintAdminArgs's `--env must be local or staging` throw (:100). P2 rather than P1: it is near-glue over a tested pure core, and a misconfiguration fails loudly on the operator's first invocation.

findings.title: Only the `minted` arm of formatMintReport is ever rendered; the operator-facing warning lines are unasserted
findings.reason: The 'Orphaned Supabase Auth identity: <id>' line (:734, :740), the dry-run 'auth.users is not readable' WARNING (:709-713) and the 'mint COMMITTED but the recovery link could not be generated' WARNING (:725-728) are all 0-covered — yet each is the ONLY channel by which the operator learns something the runbook then tells them to act on. deleteOrphanAuthUser's catch arm (:425-427) is likewise 0-covered. Operational note: the alert path itself is sound — this is an operator-run CLI with no Sentry signal and no rule row in beta-launch-alerting.md, and none is required; every terminal path is reported to stdout and mapped to a non-zero exit.

findings.title: Plan §1 cites `staging-guard.ts:65,76` as 'the includes() test'; :76 is an equality test and the includes() is at :82
findings.reason: Re-resolved against HEAD: staging-guard.ts:65 is `const ref = confirmRef.trim().toLowerCase();` and :76 is `if (ref !== KNOWN_STAGING_REF)` — an EQUALITY test whose own JSDoc at :54-55 says 'the confirmed ref must EQUAL the known staging ref'. The `includes()` the plan means is at :82 (`if (!target.includes(ref))`), with a sibling at :126. The substantive comparison the plan draws is TRUE — assertMintTarget is stricter, because it parses the ref out of each half and requires equality where staging-guard only requires substring PRESENCE in the raw target — so this is a wrong pointer, not a false design claim. Fix: cite :82 (and :126).
findings.arbiter_reasoning: P1, not P0: the claim the citation supports is verifiable and correct at :82; only the line numbers mislead. Every other path:line in the changed docs re-resolved cleanly at HEAD — 29 citations checked by hand (prevalidate-plan.py exists but is plan-shaped, so citations were resolved directly against HEAD).

findings.title: The runbook documents no exit codes, and omits the two createUser FAILED outputs from its refusal table
findings.reason: The script maps outcomes to 0 / 2 (usage) / 3 (refused) / 4 (failed) at mint-admin.ts:748-751, which is the only signal a wrapper or a runbook step can branch on, and no doc records them. The 'Refusals, and what each one means' table also omits `FAILED: Supabase createUser failed: …` and `Supabase createUser returned no user and no error`. Everything else in the runbook re-resolved correctly, including both § headings the script points operators at.
